title: Security posture discovery - Avalon Health
summary: Discovery focused on Avalon Health's security requirements for evaluating Redwood's Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments. Key concerns: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs retention, encryption/KMS, BYOK, data residency and PHI handling. Agreed next step: send security pack + SOC2, schedule technical deep dive with infra team and POC scoping.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
action_items: Owner: Maya Patel - Send Redwood security pack (SOC2 report, ISO cert summary, SOC2 controls mapping) - Due: 2026-04-15
Owner: Daniel Cho - Prepare short tech checklist for POC (network diagram, expected rps, sample dataset guidance) - Due: 2026-04-17
Owner: Tina Park (Avalon) - Share current data flow diagram and list of PHI data types - Due: 2026-04-20
next_steps: Redwood to share security pack and SOC2 redacted report
Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) with Avalon infra team for week of 20 April
Follow-up to scope POC and define success criteria for throughput/latency and data handling
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. We have Daniel and Ravi from the solutions team. Sara, Luis, Tina, thanks for your time.
[00:09] Sara Bryant: Hi, thanks. We're just trying to understand security posture across your hosted, dedicated and private options, especially for PHI workloads.
[00:20] Daniel Cho: Sure, totally. Quick agenda: compliance evidence (SOC2/ISO), auth (SSO/SAML/SCIM), RBAC, logs/retention, encryption/KMS, and then questions about network and PII/PHI.
[00:33] Luis Ortega: Good. We run patient-identifiable data in our pipelines and our legal team is strict about residency, audit trails and key management.
[00:42] Ravi Menon: Understood. High level: Hosted is our managed API with SOC2 Type II and encryption, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and private VPC peering, Private is the customer-controlled deployment (VPC or on-prem) with full control over keys and network.
[00:58] Tina Park: Do you have ISO 27001 as well? Our procurement asks for both SOC2 and ISO.
[01:06] Maya Patel: We maintain SOC2 Type II; we also have an ISO 27001 alignment summary for our control mappings - we can share certificates and evidence in the security pack.
[01:18] Sara Bryant: For SOC2, do you provide the full report or a redacted version? Also, do you do annual pen tests?
[01:26] Daniel Cho: We typically provide a redacted SOC2 report and an addendum that maps controls to our product features. Annual penetration testing is completed by a third party; results summary is in the package.
[01:40] Luis Ortega: Encryption - at rest and in transit - how is key management handled? Can we bring our own keys (BYOK) and tie into our HSM/KMS?
[01:51] Ravi Menon: For Hosted we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations in our Private offering and Dedicated with BYOK for enterprise customers. Hosted offers encryption at rest using our managed keys by default, with options for enterprise tenants to use BYOK via our KMS connectors in Dedicated/Private. We also support envelope encryption patterns and rotation policies.
[02:10] Tina Park: Is there HSM-backed key storage? We need FIPS compliance for keys.
[02:15] Daniel Cho: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we integrate with customer HSM/KMS (AWS KMS with CloudHSM or equivalent); we can supply architecture notes for FIPS validated HSMs.
[02:25] Sara Bryant: Logging and audit trails - retention and access controls are critical. What's the default retention and can we extend?
[02:33] Maya Patel: By default logs are retained 90 days in hosted analytics, but for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers you can configure retention, export logs to your SIEM, and we support long-term archival for compliance.
[02:44] Luis Ortega: Do logs include full request payloads? For PHI we can't keep payloads longer than the retention window.
[02:51] Daniel Cho: We redact sensitive fields in logs by default for hosted, but customers can control redaction rules if they run Dedicated or Private. For PCI/PHI we recommend Private or Dedicated with custom redaction and local log export to your SIEM for custody.
[03:05] Tina Park: SSO and provisioning - we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning. How's SSO setup?
[03:12] Ravi Menon: We support SAML SSO with IdPs like Okta, Azure AD, and provide SCIM for user provisioning. Role-based access (RBAC) maps SCIM groups to Redwood roles. We can show a sample SAML metadata and SCIM attribute mapping.
[03:26] Sara Bryant: Can RBAC integrate with our existing LDAP groups?
[03:30] Daniel Cho: Yes, via SCIM and SAML group mapping, or via SAML assertions. In Private deployments you can also use internal LDAP/AD directly.
[03:40] Luis Ortega: Network security - can Dedicated/Private be put inside our VPC? We need Private connectivity with no public internet egress for PHI.
[03:48] Maya Patel: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints. Private is fully customer-managed inside your VPC or on-prem - that option is recommended if you need air-gapped or zero public egress.
[04:00] Tina Park: Are there documented hardening guides for the private install?
[04:03] Ravi Menon: Yes, we maintain a Private deployment runbook with network diagrams, port requirements, firewall rules, and recommended hardening steps. We'll share that.
[04:12] Sara Bryant: Data residency - do you have EU regions and guarantees for data staying in-region?
[04:18] Daniel Cho: We host in multiple regions; for Hosted customers we have data residency options and contractual clauses. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated with region-specific pools or Private deployment inside your region.
[04:30] Luis Ortega: Our legal team will insist on data processing addendums and a BAA since PHI's involved. Do you sign BAAs?
[04:38] Maya Patel: We do sign BAAs for enterprise contracts; that's covered under our Private/Dedicated enterprise agreements.
[04:45] Tina Park: What about long-term data retention policies for embeddings and KV caches? We don't want embeddings that contain PHI to persist beyond a short retention window.
[04:55] Daniel Cho: Embeddings and KV caches are treated as transient in Hosted by default, but some caching can persist short-term to improve latency. For PHI we recommend Dedicated w/ config that disables persistent caching or Private where you control caches and retention. We can show config flags in the POC.
[05:12] Sara Bryant: Any certifications for software supply chain or dependency scanning? We run strict SBOM requirements.
[05:19] Ravi Menon: We provide SBOM summaries and vulnerability scanning reports; we can provide evidence of CI-based checks, SCA results, and dependency policies in the security package.
[05:30] Luis Ortega: Latency/cost tradeoffs - if we go Dedicated for data control, how different is the performance vs Hosted?
[05:37] Maya Patel: Dedicated is runway-optimized with reserved GPU pools which gives predictable throughput; hosted is multi-tenant and can be slightly more variable but gives faster time to value. For strict compliance Dedicated/Private are recommended for PHI.
[05:52] Tina Park: Is there a way to run a quick benchmark using our sample data?
[05:56] Daniel Cho: Yes, we can scope a POC where we run sample prompts and measure latency and throughput. We'll need a small dataset and expected qps.
[06:05] Sara Bryant: How do you handle deletion requests and data retention on delete? We have HIPAA-required deletion paths.
[06:11] Ravi Menon: We have APIs to delete customer data and can configure automated retention and purge jobs. For Hosted we provide deletion endpoints and logging of deletes; for Dedicated/Private it's plumbed into your infra, so deletion is under your control.
[06:24] Luis Ortega: Audit logs - can we stream logs to Splunk/Datadog?
[06:29] Daniel Cho: Yes, we support log shipping to Splunk/Datadog/S3 and syslog endpoints; we can also push to SIEM via secure forwarders.
[06:38] Tina Park: For compliance we need immutable audit trails and retention for 7 years for some records. Can you support long-term immutable storage?
[06:46] Maya Patel: We support long-term archival to customer-owned S3 with lock policies for immutability in Dedicated/Private. For hosted customers we have archival options but enterprise agreements cover longer retention and immutability specifics.
[07:00] Sara Bryant: Is there role separation on the Redwood side? We want to know who at Redwood can access logs and data for support.
[07:07] Daniel Cho: We have a least-privilege support model, documented access processes, and audit trails. Access requires approvals and is time-limited; all access is logged. We'll include our access policy document.
[07:20] Luis Ortega: Do you offer SSO MFA enforcement?
[07:23] Ravi Menon: SSO integrates with IdP policies so MFA enforcement is applied by the customer's IdP; we also support conditional access.
[07:31] Tina Park: Network scans - do you run periodic vulnerability scans of your infra?
[07:36] Daniel Cho: Yes, regular scans and remediation cycles. Results are summarized in our security pack.
[07:44] Sara Bryant: Any incident response SLA and post-incident reporting?
[07:49] Maya Patel: We have incident response playbooks, a security incident SLA for enterprise customers, and post-incident reports with timelines and mitigations.
[08:00] Luis Ortega: Ok, so immediate asks - send SOC2 redacted report, ISO summary, privacy/data processing addendum template, and network runbook.
[08:10] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll send those. Daniel, Ravi will put together the POC checklist.
[08:15] Daniel Cho: We'll need a technical deep dive to scope POC; recommend 60-90 minute SE-led session with your infra and network folks.
[08:24] Tina Park: That works. Also curious - for Dedicated do you allow full disk encryption at the instance level?
[08:30] Ravi Menon: Yes, disk-level encryption with customer keys is supported in Dedicated/Private; we'll include details.
[08:38] Sara Bryant: Are backups encrypted and do you have a retention policy for backups?
[08:43] Daniel Cho: Backups are encrypted and retention is configurable; we suggest short retention for PHI and show mechanisms for isolated backup stores.
[08:54] Luis Ortega: Regarding SLAs, what uptime and support tiers exist for Dedicated?
[08:59] Maya Patel: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime with enterprise support and 24/7 escalation for critical incidents; we'll include the SLA summary.
[09:10] Tina Park: Can we see a sample contract clause for data processing and audit rights?
[09:14] Maya Patel: Yes, that'll be in the legal/security package.
[09:20] Sara Bryant: What about change management - how are upgrades handled in Dedicated? We can't have unplanned downtime.
[09:27] Ravi Menon: We support scheduled maintenance windows and zero-downtime rollouts where possible; private deployments are fully customer-controlled for upgrades.
[09:36] Luis Ortega: Any rate limiting and throttling controls to prevent noisy neighbors?
[09:40] Daniel Cho: For Dedicated we provide tenant isolation with predictable quotas; for hosted we have rate limits and can offer burst policies for enterprise accounts.
[09:50] Tina Park: Are there examples of other healthcare customers using Private for PHI?
[09:55] Maya Patel: Yes, we can provide anonymized case studies and reference architecture.
[10:03] Sara Bryant: Ok let's plan the deep dive. Who will own scheduling?
[10:07] Maya Patel: I'll coordinate via email and include a proposed agenda.
[10:11] Luis Ortega: Timeline - we need a vendor selected within 6 weeks if the POC shows good results.
[10:16] Daniel Cho: Understood. We'll aim to have the POC plan within a week after the deep dive.
[10:23] Tina Park: One last question - do you support audit log immutability via WORM for certain records?
[10:29] Ravi Menon: Yes, via customer-owned S3 with object lock for Dedicated/Private; hosted has archival but we'd need enterprise addendum for WORM requirements.
[10:40] Sara Bryant: Great. Thanks everyone.
[10:42] Maya Patel: Thanks, we'll follow up with the security pack and suggested time for the SE deep dive.
[10:50] -- End of recording --
